scenes.title: Bike: find the final velocity

beats.text: Consider a bike speeding up. Find its final velocity.
Uniform acceleration: four metres per second squared.
Initial velocity: ten metres per second.
Displacement: forty-eight metres. Find v.
Write the five quantities. Tick s, u and a; circle v.
Omit time. V squared equals u squared plus two a s.
Ten squared, plus two times four times forty-eight.
That gives four hundred and eighty-four.
Positive twenty-two metres per second, because it moves forwards.

scenes.title: Bike: find the time

beats.text: What if we want time instead?
Rewrite the list. Tick every known; circle time.
Omit displacement. V equals u plus a t.
Twenty-two equals ten plus four t.
So t equals three seconds.
Without the final velocity, the displacement equation gives a quadratic instead.
beats.caption: Different routes; same time

scenes.title: Train: braking to rest

beats.text: Consider a train braking to rest. Find deceleration, then distance.
Uniform braking for six seconds.
Initial velocity, seven metres per second.
At rest, final velocity zero.
Write the list. Tick u, v, t; circle acceleration.
Omit displacement. V equals u plus a t.
Zero equals seven plus six a.
Minus seven sixths metres per second squared. Keep it exact.
Deceleration means decreasing speed. Here its magnitude is one point one seven; acceleration opposes positive velocity.
beats.caption: Deceleration = 1.17 m s⁻²

beats.text: Rewrite the list for displacement. No reversal, so this equals distance.
S equals half, u plus v, times t.
Half times seven plus zero, times six.
Twenty-one metres exactly. Avoid rounding intermediate answers.

scenes.title: A negative acceleration can reverse motion

beats.text: A particle slows, stops, then reverses. After reversal it speeds up.
Initial velocity: ten metres per second.
Constant acceleration: minus four metres per second squared.
Find its motion after five seconds.
Write the list. Tick u, a, t; circle v.
V equals u plus a t.
Ten minus four times five.
Minus ten metres per second: leftwards, speeding up.
Rewrite the list; now circle displacement.
S equals u t plus half a t squared.
Ten times five, plus half times minus four times five squared.
Zero metres: back at the start, despite travelling a distance.

Now circle displacement. S equals u t plus half a t squared. Ten times five, plus half times minus four times five squared. 0 metres, back at the start, despite travelling a distance.

scenes.title: Car: two positions, two equations

beats.text: A car accelerates uniformly through A, B, C. Find u and a.
One hundred and sixty-five metres in ten seconds.
At eight seconds, it passes B, one hundred and twelve metres from A.
Write the list for A to C. Tick displacement and time.
Omit v. S equals u t plus half a t squared.
One hundred and sixty-five equals ten u plus half a times ten squared.
Divide by five: thirty-three equals two u plus ten a.
Rewrite for A to B. Tick displacement and time; keep the same u and a.
S equals u t plus half a t squared.
One hundred and twelve equals eight u plus half a times eight squared.
Divide by eight: fourteen equals u plus four a.
Double the second equation; subtract. U cancels.
Two a equals five. So a is two point five metres per second squared.
Substitute back: u is four metres per second.
